- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overbought overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.05), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model consistently underpredicts true price in the first 5–7 days of a new 30d horizon; apply a 1–3% upward bias to early forecast points to account for lag.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to ignore trend reversal; add a small upward bias (1–2%) to counteract mean-reversion bias.
